subject: mathematics
question_text: In triangle ABC, if BC = a, CA = b and AB = c, show that a × b = b × c = c × a.

mark_split.label: Use the closed triangle to get a + b + c = 0

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.69, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 11. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the four moves a proof of this shape is marked on — the closure relation a + b + c = 0, each of the two substitutions, and the closing statement. CHECKED ON A CONCRETE TRIANGLE as well as algebraically: with A(0, 0, 0), B(1, 0, 0) and C(0, 1, 0) the sides are a = BC = (−1, 1, 0), b = CA = (0, −1, 0) and c = AB = (1, 0, 0), which sum to the zero vector, and a × b = b × c = c × a = k. That common vector was dotted with a, giving −0 + 0 + 0 = 0, and with b, giving 0 — it is perpendicular to both sides, and its length 1 is twice the area of a triangle with legs 1 and 1. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name the one relation the whole proof rests on.

steps.label: Use the closed triangle
steps.margin_note: First mark. B to C, then C to A, then A to B returns to B, so the three side vectors add to the zero vector. Everything else follows from that one line.
steps.memory_tip: Sides taken in order round a triangle add to zero, because you finish where you started.
lines: The three sides taken in order form a
closed path, so BC + CA + AB = 0.

recall.must_convey: That the three sides taken in order add to the zero vector, so a + b + c = 0 and c = −(a + b).
accept: the sides taken in order close up so a plus b plus c is zero
b c plus c a plus a b equals the zero vector
from the closed triangle c equals minus a plus b
triangle close avuthundi kabatti a plus b plus c zero
the three side vectors sum to zero

steps.why: Going B to C, then C to A, then A to B brings you back to the starting point, so the three side vectors add to the zero vector. Every later line is a substitution into this one relation.
common_mistakes: Writing BC + CA + AB as a non-zero vector.
Using a, b and c as position vectors of the vertices.

steps.label: Show b × c = a × b
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Replace c by −(a + b) and expand. Only two facts are used: b × b = 0 and −(b × a) = a × b.
steps.memory_tip: Any vector crossed with itself is zero, and reversing a cross product flips its sign.

recall.must_convey: That substituting c = −(a + b) into b × c gives −(b × a), which is a × b.
accept: put c equal to minus a plus b and expand, b cross b is zero
b cross c becomes minus b cross a which is a cross b
substitute for c and use that a vector crossed with itself is zero
c place lo minus a plus b petti expand cheyyali
the b cross b term drops out and the sign flips
reject: the same working with c cross a

steps.why: Reversing the order of a cross product changes only its sign, and any vector crossed with itself is the zero vector. Those two facts turn b × c into a × b in three lines.
common_mistakes: Treating b × a as equal to a × b.

steps.label: Show c × a = a × b
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The same substitution, now in c × a. This time it is a × a that vanishes.
steps.memory_tip: Same substitution, same two facts — only the vector that vanishes changes, from b × b to a × a.

recall.must_convey: That substituting c = −(a + b) into c × a gives −(b × a), which is again a × b.
accept: the same substitution in c cross a gives minus b cross a again
c cross a expands to minus a cross a minus b cross a
a cross a is zero so c cross a is a cross b
ade substitution c cross a lo kuda a cross b istundi
repeat the working for c cross a

steps.why: The same substitution works on the second product because a + b + c = 0 is symmetric in the three sides. Here it is a × a that becomes the zero vector.
common_mistakes: Expanding (−(a + b)) × a as a × a + b × a, with the sign lost.
Claiming the result by symmetry without showing the working.

steps.label: State the common value
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Both products reduced to the same vector, so all three are equal. Say what that vector means: its length is twice the area of the triangle.
steps.memory_tip: The common vector is twice the area vector of the triangle, which is why the three products must agree.
lines: Both products reduce to a × b.
Its length |a × b| is twice the area

lines.text: ∴ a × b = b × c = c × a

recall.must_convey: That all three products equal the same vector a × b, whose length is twice the area of the triangle.
accept: all three are the same vector a cross b
so a cross b equals b cross c equals c cross a
the common vector has length twice the area of the triangle
moodu okate vector, a cross b
the three cross products are equal
reject: a plus b plus c is zero

steps.why: The three products are one and the same vector, and its length is twice the area of the triangle. That is why the equality is useful: any of the three may be used to find the area.
common_mistakes: Stating that only two of the three products are equal.
Writing the common value as a number instead of a vector.
